items.name: bui
items.title: Beautiful UI primitives
items.description: Beautiful UI's primitives (MIT) as pikit's dashboard has them, fed by real data: the sidebar, the composer (its plus, slash and assistant menus), thinking, tool chips, context cards, an operator's page, records tables, filter chips, status dots, badges, buttons, switches, a combobox, a code block. They use the tokens and classes of the dashboard's src/index.css.

items.name: admin-proposals-settings
items.title: admin-proposals-settings
items.description: admin-proposals's section of the Settings dialog: The dashboard's side of the agent's changes to itself: the proposals that `proposals` holds (proposals-local on a server, proposals-github on Cloudflare) listed with their diff and checks, approved or rejected there by an operator; and a Settings section saying whether they can be made and approved now, with the deploys that follow. Its settings come with the component (pikit add admin-proposals), stored by settings-store.

items.name: admin-proposals
items.title: admin-proposals
items.description: admin-proposals's view: The dashboard's side of the agent's changes to itself: the proposals that `proposals` holds (proposals-local on a server, proposals-github on Cloudflare) listed with their diff and checks, approved or rejected there by an operator; and a Settings section saying whether they can be made and approved now, with the deploys that follow. Its admin API routes come with the component (pikit add admin-proposals).

items.name: agents-live-settings
items.title: agents-live-settings
items.description: agents-live's section of the Settings dialog: Agents as data: an operator creates, edits and removes agents (name, description, prompt, model, tools, extensions) in the dashboard's Settings, provided as agent.directory; with router-rules, routed to live. Its settings come with the component (pikit add agents-live), stored by settings-store.

items.name: channel-google-chat-settings
items.title: channel-google-chat-settings
items.description: channel-google-chat's section of the Settings dialog: A Google Chat app of your own (a Workspace add-on) answers in each message's thread: Thinking… written as the model writes, tables and code as cards, photos and files read, questions asked with buttons and forms. On a server or on Cloudflare. Its settings come with the component (pikit add channel-google-chat), stored by settings-store.

items.name: channel-web-settings
items.title: channel-web-settings
items.description: channel-web's section of the Settings dialog: A chat page for people who are not operators: they sign in (email and password, a link by email, Google, GitHub or any OIDC platform), see and continue only their own conversations, watch the answer as it is written, attach images and stop a run. The operator invites, bans and removes them. On Cloudflare the Worker serves it, each conversation in its Durable Object, the accounts in one object. Its settings come with the component (pikit add channel-web), stored by settings-store.

items.name: channel-web
items.title: channel-web
items.description: channel-web's view: A chat page for people who are not operators: they sign in (email and password, a link by email, Google, GitHub or any OIDC platform), see and continue only their own conversations, watch the answer as it is written, attach images and stop a run. The operator invites, bans and removes them. On Cloudflare the Worker serves it, each conversation in its Durable Object, the accounts in one object. Its admin API routes come with the component (pikit add channel-web).

items.name: health-registry
items.title: health-registry
items.description: health-registry's view: What is up, degraded or down: components report their own state; /health fails when an essential one stays down, so the supervisor restarts the process. Its admin API routes come with the component (pikit add health-registry).

items.name: repo-github-app-settings
items.title: repo-github-app-settings
items.description: repo-github-app's section of the Settings dialog: Connects the project's GitHub repository in two clicks from the dashboard's Settings → GitHub: a GitHub App created in your account from a manifest and installed on the repository, whose short-lived installation tokens the app mints itself (`repo.github`), its credentials sealed at rest. No token is pasted anywhere. Its settings come with the component (pikit add repo-github-app), stored by settings-store.

items.name: repo-github-token-settings
items.title: repo-github-token-settings
items.description: repo-github-token's section of the Settings dialog: The project's GitHub access (`repo.github`) from a fine-grained token you made, the GITHUB_TOKEN secret, and the repository, a setting changed in the dashboard's Settings → GitHub: for a project run from the CLI or on a server. Its settings come with the component (pikit add repo-github-token), stored by settings-store.

items.name: router-basic-settings
items.title: router-basic-settings
items.description: router-basic's section of the Settings dialog: Every message goes to one agent: `defaultAgent`. Its settings come with the component (pikit add router-basic), stored by settings-store.

items.name: router-rules-settings
items.title: router-rules-settings
items.description: router-rules's section of the Settings dialog: Each conversation goes to the agent of the first rule it matches: rules in config, edited live from the dashboard. Its settings come with the component (pikit add router-rules), stored by settings-store.

items.name: runtime-pi-settings
items.title: runtime-pi-settings
items.description: runtime-pi's section of the Settings dialog: The agent runtime: Pi runs your agents, and this component plugs it into the app. Its settings come with the component (pikit add runtime-pi), stored by settings-store.
